description: We’re an Arab team building “Mars in Arabia”, an interactive map that discovers new Mars and Moon analog sites in the Saudi desert (lava fields, lava tubes, dunes and craters) and scores each one using real NASA Earth, Mars and Moon data.
summary: Mars in Arabia is an interactive 3D website that proposes Saudi Arabian sites as field analogs for permanent Moon and Mars bases. We scanned 36,300 cells across the Arabian Peninsula using NASA elevation, vegetation and climate data, then studied six field sites in depth: Harrat Khaybar, the Umm Jirsan lava tube, Harrat Rahat, the Rub' al Khali, Al Wahbah crater and the Wabar impact craters. Each site is shown in real 3D next to its Mars or Moon twin, built from NASA MOLA and LOLA elevation data. Each site is scored on geology, terrain, aridity and temperature swing, and linked to an Artemis III south-pole region and a proposed Mars base zone it could help crews train for. This matters because most analog training happens in a few places like the Atacama, Iceland and Hawaii, while Arabia's young lava fields, lava tubes, craters and the world's largest sand sea remain rarely used. Our tool gives mission planners a data-backed shortlist with field seasons and access already worked out, and every number shows its source.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Mars in Arabia is an interactive 3D website that finds and explains places in Saudi Arabia where crews could train for permanent Moon and Mars bases.

1. Analog Finder: scans the whole Arabian Peninsula on a 0.1° grid (36,300 cells). Each cell is scored for three analog types (volcanic, smooth plains, rugged) using SRTM elevation (slope and relief), NASA MODIS NDVI (bare ground) and NASA POWER rainfall. It checks itself against our six known sites and suggests new, unstudied candidates such as Harrat Uwayrid, Ithnayn, Hammah and Lunayyir.

2. Six field sites in 3D: Harrat Khaybar, the Umm Jirsan lava tube, Harrat Rahat (1256 CE lava flow), the Rub' al Khali dune sea, Al Wahbah crater and the Wabar impact craters. Each is real terrain draped with Sentinel-2 imagery. One click swaps it for its Mars or Moon twin, built from NASA MOLA or LOLA elevation (Tharsis/Arsia Mons, Elysium, Nili Patera, Meridiani Planum, Marius Hills, Linné crater).

3. Measured analog score (0-100): Geology 35% (rock class from the USGS geologic map of Mars and a world geology map, plus a cited landform match), Terrain 25% (Earth vs twin elevation compared at the same pixel size: slope distribution, roughness, relief), Aridity 25% (NASA POWER rain) and Thermal swing 15% (NASA POWER ground temperature vs the twin's surface range).

4. Evidence for each site: a side-by-side table, a cross-section, a slope-mix chart, monthly ground temperature, and a field-test plan (best season, nearest city, driveable ground).

5. Base relevance: each site is linked to an Artemis III south-pole candidate region and a proposed Mars base zone (Jezero, Gale, Meridiani Planum or the Hebrus Valles pits), with what crews would rehearse there.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Most analog training happens in a few places (Atacama, Iceland, Hawaii, Utah). Arabia has the world's largest sand sea and huge young basalt fields with lava tubes and craters, and it is easy to reach. Our tool gives mission planners and Saudi and regional space agencies a data-backed shortlist of training sites, with field seasons and access already worked out. It also helps students and the public in the Arab world see their own land as part of space exploration.

CREATIVITY

Instead of a static map, judges and users can fly from Earth to Arabia, watch it turn into Mars, and switch any Saudi site into its real Mars or Moon twin on the same 3D block. The comparison is measured, not just visual.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Geology, terrain, aridity, temperature, access, safety and field seasons (heat). We were also honest about limits: no place on Earth matches Mars or Moon gravity, air pressure or radiation. The website has a "How sure we are" section covering data resolution, approximate positions, and which parts are our own proposals.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript; three.js (WebGL 3D), GSAP and Lenis (animation), Leaflet (maps); Python (numpy, Pillow, pyshp) for the data pipeline; hosted on GitHub Pages.
